_meta.name: OODA MAS Thesis Policy Database
_meta.purpose: Defines behavioral constraints and optimization objective of the Multi-Agent System. Strategist uses this for bid reasoning; budget changes are governed by Zupervisor-only baseline trigger rules. Numeric values align with logic/optimization.py.

optimization_objective.description: Primary objective: maximize business value from leads while keeping acquisition efficient and budget pacing healthy.
optimization_objective.plain_language_summary: The objective rewards lead generation, penalizes expensive conversion, penalizes wasteful spend when conversion quality deteriorates, penalizes spend with zero leads, and rewards spending close to the time-adjusted hourly target.
optimization_objective.utility_definition: Utility is lead value minus inefficiency and waste penalties.

objective_breakdown.utility_component: Net business value from outcomes (lead value - CPA penalty - leakage penalty - no-conversion penalty).
objective_breakdown.pacing_component: Spending discipline term: reward on-target spend, stronger penalty for overspend, weighted by time-of-day urgency.

decision_intuition: More leads at acceptable CPA should increase bids or maintain them.
High CPA above target should reduce score and push toward tighter bidding.
When CPA is high and CVR is weak, spend is likely low quality and should be penalized strongly.
Spending with no leads is treated as avoidable overhead.
Late-day under-delivery is more costly than early-day under-delivery due to higher pacing urgency.

volume_score.explanation: Each lead contributes business value. Baseline value is CHF 500 per lead, with an extra CHF 100 bonus during confirmed holiday windows to reflect higher strategic opportunity.

cpa_penalty.explanation: Only above-target CPA is penalized. The penalty scales with lead volume, so costly acquisition at scale is penalized more than small fluctuations.

leakage_penalty.logic: Leakage penalty activates only when both efficiency and quality are poor: CPA is above target and CVR is below baseline. This captures spend that is expensive and low quality.

no_conversion_penalty.formula: KAPPA × spend  (only when leads == 0 AND spend > 0)
no_conversion_penalty.explanation: If spend occurs with zero leads, 20% of spend is penalized as overhead. This discourages silent budget burn even when other penalties do not activate.

pacing_score.formula: λ × min(spend, target) − OVERSPEND_FACTOR × λ × max(spend − target, 0)
pacing_score.lambda: exp(current_hour_in_day / 24) — shadow price of budget utilisation
pacing_score.explanation: Pacing rewards spending near the volatility-adjusted hourly target and penalizes overspending more heavily than it rewards spend. Time-of-day urgency rises later in the day, so late pacing misses matter more.

variable_meanings.actual_spend: Total spend observed in the decision window.
variable_meanings.target_spend: Expected spend for that window based on daily budget and volatility regime.
variable_meanings.lambda: Time-of-day urgency weight. Low early day, higher late day.
variable_meanings.overspend_factor: Asymmetry multiplier (2.0) so overspending is punished more strongly.

sign_intuition: If spend is on or below target, pacing score is non-negative and increases with lambda.
If spend exceeds target, overspend penalty grows quickly because it is multiplied by overspend_factor and lambda.
During crash (volatility=0), target_spend becomes zero, so any positive spend is treated as overspend.
worked_examples: Normal hour: spend near target => positive pacing contribution.
Late-day underspend: lower immediate penalty than overspend, but missed reward is larger because lambda is high.
Crash hour: spend=0 => pacing ~0; spend>0 => negative pacing.

policy_logic: If CPA slightly above target → reduce bids gradually.
If CPA significantly above target → reduce bids aggressively.
If CPA remains above hard threshold for multiple hours → escalate.

budget_pacing_policy.objective: Spend the full daily budget without large hourly deviations.
budget_pacing_policy.budget_governance: Zupervisor only. Strategist and Taskmaster do not execute budget changes.
policy_logic: Early in the day → prioritise CPA efficiency (λ ≈ 1).
Late in the day → prioritise spending remaining budget (λ >> 1).
Avoid large underspending unless CPA protection requires it.
Budget changes are applied only by Zupervisor through baseline-equivalent trigger checks.
If CVR drops moderately → reduce bids.
If CVR drops severely → pause campaign to prevent leakage.
If CVR surges significantly → increase bids cautiously (OPPORTUNITY mode).
Confirm volatility over multiple hours before major actions.
Market silence caused by sub-market bids (max_bid ≤ 0.80 CHF) is NOT a CVR drop.
After emergency bid-pause: Taskmaster applies a CHF 2.00 recovery floor on the first non-emergency cycle to restore market competitiveness quickly.

conditions_for_escalation: CPA above 120 for more than 3 hours.
Campaign paused for more than 6 hours.
escalation_policy.purpose: Prevent autonomous drift and maintain stakeholder trust.

policy_logic: Do not react to single-hour anomalies.
Require persistence before large bid or pause decisions.
Near-zero activity when max_bid ≤ 0.80 CHF is bid-induced silence, not a structural market failure.

execution_constraints.description: All actions must stay within safe operational bounds. The Taskmaster enforces these programmatically after every LLM decision.

transparency_policy.purpose: Ensure explainability and stakeholder trust. All five glass-box reasoning layers are mandatory.
